Commentary.Commentary: 297 is the target! England will fancy themselves to chase this down but it won't be that easy. Can they do so? Join us in a while to find out.

The England bowling was decent throughout. Wood and Curran started off well before the former walked off due to an injury. The two spinners fared decently. Liam Plunkett, despite being expensive was the pick as he finished with a four-fer.

The Australia innings was all about one man - Steven Smith. It was his hundred which has taken them to the position they are in. The rest of the batters did get starts but nothing significant. Everybody who batted with Smith, played around him and he was the anchor. Had any other batsman, converted their start, Australia would have posted a big first innings score.
So Australia have ended with a score they will be pleased with. however, England too won't be disappointed with what they have to chase. The game is evenly poised as we head into the break.

OUT! RUN OUT! So a single and a wicket to end the innings! Zampa hits it towards deep mid-wicket and the batters take one. Zampa wants another and he runs towards the keeper's end. The fielder throws it to the keeper and then Buttler fires it to the bowler who whips the bails off. AUSTRALIA END WITH 297!

OUT! A very harsh call one cay say, probably the soft signal played a big, big part there. Curran bowls a yorker on middle, Smith looks to flick it but it goes back towards the bowler who takes it and appeals. The umpires get together and then take it upstairs. The SOFT SIGNAL IS OUT! Replays roll in and there is nothing very conclusive, the umpire after a few replays rules it in the favor of the bowler. End of a magnificent innings Smith. He has probably single handledly taken Australia to where they are at the moment.
Is that a catch? The umpires are not sure and they have taken it upstairs to check if it has bounced or directly on the boot. Smith has already started walking back and the SOFT SIGNAL IS ALSO OUT!
Creams it to sweeper cover but does not take a run again. The last time he did so, he smashed a biggie on the next ball.

On the stumps this time, Warner gets right behind the line and defends it.
Angles this away from the off pole to the left-hander. Warner makes a leave.
On the pads, Finch flicks it uppishly but towards fine leg so only a run. Australia and Finch are underway!
Back of a length again on off, Finch stands tall and keeps it out.

NOT OUT! Umpire's call! It is clipping the leg pole. England don't lose the review though. Curran lands it on a length around middle, this one comes back in. Finch looks to flick but misses. Gets hit on the pads. An appeal and the umpire shakes his head. Buttler reviews and replays show that the on-field call is the right one.
Action straightaway! A review by England for an LBW. Finch is the man in question. Looks close.
Tom Curran to bowl from the other end!
A good nut to end a maiden over by Wood to begin with. In the 5th stump channel. Warner lunges and makes a leave.
Bowls it short again and this one bounces at a good height. Warner stands tall and keeps it out.
BEATEN! Slightly short and around off, Warner looks to pull it but the ball does not bonce as much as he expected it to. It sneaks under the bat and Buttler behind collects it with a dive.

Perfect line and length! Starts on off and it comes back in. It is on a length once again, Warner pushes it to the right of the bowler. Finch wants a run but is sent back. Wood gets to the ball quickly and has a shy at his end but misses.
This one swings in a little but the line is a little too straight, Warner looks to flick but misses to get hit high on the pads.
A good start by both, the batsman as well as the bowler. Wood lands it on a length and around off, Warner goes back and punches it right off the middle to covers.
The players and the umpires make their way out to the middle. Aaron Finch and David Warner are the openers for Australia. Mark Wood will start the proceedings for the hosts. Here we go...

Australia - Aaron Finch (C), David Warner, Steven Smith, Usman Khawaja, Glenn Maxwell, Alex Carey (WK), Shaun Marsh, Marcus Stoinis, Kane Richardson, Nathan Lyon, Mitchell Starc, Pat Cummins, Adam Zampa, Nathan Coulter-Nile, Jason Behrendorff.
England - James Vince, Jonny Bairstow, Joe Root, Jos Buttler (WK/C), Ben Stokes, Moeen Ali, Chris Woakes, Jason Roy, Tom Curran, Adil Rashid, Liam Plunkett, Mark Wood, Jofra Archer, Liam Dawson.
TOSS - England win the toss and elected to field.

Hello and welcome to the 3rd Warm-up of the World Cup 2019. It's between two off cricket's oldest rivals, England and Australia. The two enter the tournament in good form and would want to continue that. This game though is a chance for them to find out their perfect combination for the big event. Despite it being a warm-up, both the sides would be eager to win it. Toss and team updates coming up shortly.
